groups.label: Making proteins
groups.plain: Machines that read a messenger RNA and build the protein it codes for.

groups.label: Reading genes
groups.plain: Machines that copy a gene's DNA into RNA.

groups.label: Copying and mending DNA
groups.plain: Machines that copy a cell's DNA before it divides, hold its strands and mend them.

groups.label: Making ATP
groups.plain: Machines that make the cell's fuel from a flow of ions across a membrane.

groups.label: Capturing light
groups.plain: Machines of the chloroplast that catch light, make ATP and NADPH from it, and fix carbon dioxide.

groups.label: Moving ions: units of the law inventory
groups.plain: Channels, pumps, exchangers and junctions: the units of the engine's law inventory that are protein assemblies, as the Protein atlas lists them. A unit's panel says which of its laws an active model declares.

groups.label: Putting proteins into membranes
groups.plain: Channels that thread new proteins across a membrane or set them into it.

groups.label: Folding proteins
groups.plain: Cages and rings that give a new protein a closed space to fold in, using ATP.

groups.label: Breaking proteins down
groups.plain: Proteases that unfold proteins and cut them, using ATP.

groups.label: Moving, sensing and attaching
groups.plain: Machines that move the cell, steer it, or hold it to a surface.

groups.label: Binding and stress response
groups.plain: Proteins that bind ions or sugars, or are associated with a stress response.

groups.label: Electron transfer
groups.plain: Proteins that pass electrons between molecules.

groups.label: Carrying cargo
groups.plain: Motors that walk along the cell's filaments, carrying cargo from place to place.

groups.label: Particles whose job is not known
groups.plain: Large particles whose function has not been found.

kinds.label: Proteasome
kinds.plain: A barrel that unfolds proteins marked for destruction and cuts them into short pieces, using ATP.

kinds.label: Ribosome
kinds.plain: Reads a messenger RNA and joins amino acids, one at a time, into the protein it codes for.

kinds.label: RNA polymerase
kinds.plain: Copies a gene's DNA into RNA, the first step from a gene to a protein.

kinds.label: ATP synthase
kinds.plain: Turns as ions flow through it across a membrane, and makes ATP as it turns; run the other way, it spends ATP to pump ions out.

records.says: Decided 17 November 2026 (D209): the ATP synthase is to be the first machine built in the engine (M1), as general pieces, after the core-seams pass; its law is to be D193's proton_coupled_atp_synthesis_cycle@1, built by the mitochondria lane. There is no model of it yet.

kinds.label: Protein translocon
kinds.plain: A channel in the membrane that threads a new protein across it, or opens sideways to set it into the membrane.

kinds.label: FtsH protease
kinds.plain: A protease that stands in the cell membrane and unfolds and cuts proteins, using ATP.

kinds.label: Lon protease
kinds.plain: A protease that unfolds and cuts proteins inside the cell, using ATP.

kinds.label: HslUV protease
kinds.plain: A barrel of HslV that cuts proteins, capped by a ring of HslU that unfolds them and feeds them in, using ATP. HslV's subunits carry the signature of the proteasome's.

kinds.label: Flagellar motor
kinds.plain: The rotary motor at the foot of each flagellum. A rotor of rings sits in the inner membrane; stator units round it let protons into the cell and push on it; a straight drive shaft passes through the wall and the outer membrane to a flexible hook, which turns the long filament.

kinds.label: Chemoreceptor array
kinds.plain: A lattice of receptor proteins in the membrane that senses chemicals and steers the cell's swimming toward food.

kinds.label: Attachment organelle
kinds.plain: A membrane protrusion at one pole with an internal core: it carries the adhesins that hold the cell to a surface, and leads the cell when it glides.

kinds.label: Nucleus
kinds.plain: Holds the cell's DNA inside a double membrane, the nuclear envelope, whose pores let molecules in and out; the nucleolus inside it is where ribosomes are put together.

kinds.label: Endoplasmic reticulum
kinds.plain: A network of membrane sheets and tubes that runs on from the nuclear envelope: the rough sheets, studded with ribosomes, make proteins for membranes and for export, and the network stores calcium.

kinds.label: Golgi apparatus
kinds.plain: Stacks of flattened sacs, the cisternae, where proteins made at the endoplasmic reticulum are modified, sorted and sent on in vesicles.

kinds.label: Mitochondrion
kinds.plain: An organelle of two membranes, the inner one folded into cristae, where most of a cell's ATP is made.

kinds.label: Chloroplast
kinds.plain: A plant cell's organelle of light: two envelope membranes round stacks of membrane discs, where photosynthesis captures light and fixes carbon dioxide.

kinds.label: Vacuole
kinds.plain: A plant cell's large sac of water and solutes, bounded by one membrane: it fills most of the cell and holds it taut against its wall.

kinds.label: Lysosome
kinds.plain: A sac of digestive enzymes in an acid lumen, bounded by one membrane, where the cell breaks down what it takes in and its own worn parts.

kinds.label: COPI vesicle
kinds.plain: A small vesicle coated with coatomer (COPI) that carries cargo between the Golgi's cisternae and back to the endoplasmic reticulum.

kinds.label: Peroxisome
kinds.plain: A small organelle of one membrane where fatty acids are broken down and hydrogen peroxide is made and destroyed.

kinds.label: Lipid droplet
kinds.plain: A store of fat in the cytoplasm: neutral lipids wrapped in a single layer of phospholipids, from which the cell draws fatty acids and sterols.

kinds.label: Autophagosome
kinds.plain: A sphere of two membranes that closes round worn parts of the cell and other cargo and carries them to a lysosome, where they are broken down (autophagy).

kinds.label: Centriole
kinds.plain: A short barrel of nine triplets of microtubules. Two of them at right angles, in a cloud of protein, make the centrosome, which organises the cell's microtubules.

kinds.label: Endocytic vesicle
kinds.plain: A small vesicle or short tubule of membrane taken in from the cell's surface and marked by the protein Rab5: among the first stations of the way in (endocytosis), before the early endosome.

kinds.label: Tat translocase
kinds.plain: Carries proteins that are already folded across the membrane.

kinds.label: BAM complex
kinds.plain: Folds new barrel-shaped proteins into a bacterium's outer membrane.

kinds.label: Signal recognition particle
kinds.plain: Catches a new protein's signal as it leaves the ribosome and brings it to the translocon.

kinds.label: Chaperonin (GroEL-GroES)
kinds.plain: Two rings that close a lid over a new protein and let it fold inside, using ATP.

kinds.label: Clp protease
kinds.plain: A ring that unfolds proteins, using ATP, and feeds them into a chamber that cuts them.

kinds.label: Complex I (NADH dehydrogenase)
kinds.plain: Takes electrons from NADH and uses their energy to pump protons across the membrane.

kinds.label: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase)
kinds.plain: Takes electrons from succinate into the chain that drives the proton pumps.

kinds.label: Cytochrome bo3 oxidase
kinds.plain: Hands electrons to oxygen at the end of a bacterium's chain and pumps protons as it does.

kinds.label: DNA polymerase III
kinds.plain: Copies the bacterial chromosome: a clamp holds it on the DNA while it adds letters at speed.

kinds.label: UvrABC excinuclease
kinds.plain: Finds a damaged stretch of DNA and cuts it out, so it can be filled in afresh.

kinds.label: RecBCD
kinds.plain: Unwinds and trims a broken DNA end so that the break can be mended from the other copy.

kinds.label: RNA degradosome
kinds.plain: A gathering of enzymes that breaks messenger RNAs down when they are no longer needed.

kinds.label: Mitochondrial ribosome
kinds.plain: The ribosome inside a mitochondrion, which makes the few proteins the mitochondrion's own DNA codes for.

kinds.label: RNA polymerase I
kinds.plain: Copies the genes of the ribosome's large RNAs into RNA.

kinds.label: RNA polymerase III
kinds.plain: Copies the genes of small RNAs, such as transfer RNAs and the ribosome's smallest RNA.

kinds.label: Complex III (cytochrome bc1)
kinds.plain: Passes electrons along the chain and pumps protons as it does.

kinds.label: Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase)
kinds.plain: Hands the electrons to oxygen, making water, and pumps protons as it does.

kinds.label: Oligosaccharyltransferase
kinds.plain: Adds a chain of sugars to a new protein as it enters the endoplasmic reticulum.

kinds.label: ER membrane protein complex
kinds.plain: Helps set new proteins into the membrane of the endoplasmic reticulum.

kinds.label: TOM complex
kinds.plain: The gate in the mitochondrion's outer membrane through which almost all its proteins enter.

kinds.label: TIM23 complex
kinds.plain: Threads proteins through the mitochondrion's inner membrane into its interior.

kinds.label: TIM22 complex
kinds.plain: Sets carrier proteins into the mitochondrion's inner membrane.

kinds.label: Nuclear pore
kinds.plain: A large gate in the nuclear envelope through which proteins and RNAs pass in and out of the nucleus.

kinds.label: Chaperonin TRiC (CCT)
kinds.plain: A double ring of eight different subunits in which many of the cell's proteins fold.

kinds.label: V-type ATPase
kinds.plain: A rotary pump that spends ATP to pump protons into a compartment and make it acid.

kinds.label: Cytoplasmic dynein
kinds.plain: Walks along microtubules toward the cell's centre, carrying cargo.

kinds.label: Dynactin
kinds.plain: A short filament that ties cytoplasmic dynein to its cargo and keeps it walking.

kinds.label: Axonemal dynein
kinds.plain: The motor that bends a cilium or a sperm's tail, by sliding its microtubules past each other.

kinds.label: Myosin II
kinds.plain: The motor that pulls on actin filaments to make a muscle contract or a cell pinch in two.

kinds.label: CMG helicase
kinds.plain: A ring that unwinds the DNA double helix ahead of the polymerases that copy it.

kinds.label: Origin recognition complex
kinds.plain: Marks the places on the chromosomes where copying the DNA starts.

kinds.label: Cohesin
kinds.plain: A ring that holds the two copies of a chromosome together until the cell divides.

kinds.label: Condensin
kinds.plain: A ring that folds a chromosome into a compact rod before the cell divides.

kinds.label: RNA exosome
kinds.plain: A barrel that unwinds RNA and cuts it down, to trim RNAs or break them up.

kinds.label: Mediator
kinds.plain: A large bridge between the proteins that switch a gene on and the polymerase that reads it.

kinds.label: Spliceosome
kinds.plain: Cuts the pieces that code for nothing out of a gene's first RNA copy and joins the rest.

kinds.label: Vault
kinds.plain: A hollow, barrel-shaped particle of protein and RNA, among the largest in a cell. What it does has not been found.
kinds.identity: Decided 19 November 2026: the vault is a named exception to how a kind is identified. The Gene Ontology has no term for it and UniProt no keyword, so its proteins are not found by a term. They are found by three footings, kept apart: the Complex Portal's entry of the species whose name holds the word vault (by record); the saved reviewed UniProt entries of the species whose FUNCTION or SUBUNIT sentences name the vault particle, found by that rule, each sentence with the evidence it carries (named by a reviewed entry); and the proteins of the species' own table that carry the signature of the major vault protein family or the PARP4 marker (candidates by family). No other kind changes its identity.
kinds.absence: A signature not found in a species is not an absence: it says what was looked for in that species' table, and nothing says the species has no vault.

kinds.label: Chloroplast ATP synthase
kinds.plain: The ATP synthase of the chloroplast, turned by the protons that the light reactions pump.

kinds.label: Chloroplast ribosome
kinds.plain: The ribosome inside a chloroplast, which makes the proteins the chloroplast's own DNA codes for.

kinds.label: Photosystem I
kinds.plain: Catches light and uses its energy to pass electrons on to make NADPH.

kinds.label: Photosystem II
kinds.plain: Catches light and uses its energy to split water, releasing oxygen.

kinds.label: Cytochrome b6f complex
kinds.plain: Passes electrons between the two photosystems and pumps protons as it does.

kinds.label: Rubisco
kinds.plain: The enzyme that fixes carbon dioxide from the air into sugar.

kinds.label: Myosin II regulatory domain
kinds.plain: Two light chains wrap around a short segment of the myosin II heavy-chain neck. The resolved region measures 63 residues on the heavy-chain construct. The motor head and tail lie outside this structure.

kinds.label: Fragmin P domains
kinds.plain: The F2 and F3 domains of the actin-binding protein fragmin P are shown together. The related depositions capture different ion conditions.

kinds.label: Actin–fragmin F1 complex
kinds.plain: The reference crystal pairs the F1 domain of Physarum fragmin with chicken skeletal actin. Other deposits include human actin. The structures show how the isolated domain binds actin.

kinds.label: Actin–fragmin kinase
kinds.plain: The resolved catalytic domain belongs to a kinase that phosphorylates actin in the actin–fragmin complex.

kinds.label: Calcium-binding protein CBP40
kinds.plain: CBP40, also called LAV1-2, forms aggregates in the presence of calcium at sites of damage to the plasmodium. This assembly is the metal-free construct. The calcium-bound structure is also listed.

kinds.label: Haemagglutinin I
kinds.plain: A lectin from Physarum. The deposited assembly contains two copies of the same protein chain.

kinds.label: Spherulin-3A
kinds.plain: A βγ-crystallin family protein associated with the spherule stage. The surface shows the four-chain assembly assigned to the crystal structure. A solution NMR entry is also listed.

kinds.label: NADH–cytochrome b5 reductase
kinds.plain: This flavoprotein transfers electrons from NADH to cytochrome b5. The surface includes both protein chains in the deposited dimer.

kinds.label: Homing endonuclease I-PpoI
kinds.plain: This Physarum endonuclease is deposited in several experimental complexes with nucleic acids. The reference assembly shows two protein chains and four DNA strands.
